pageTitle: Baritone Guitars: Go Lower, Go Deeper
subtitle: Explore the deep, powerful world of extended-range guitars

introduction.title: Baritone Guitars: Go Lower, Go Deeper
introduction.text: Discover the rich, powerful tones that only extended scale lengths and lower tunings can provide. From thunderous metal riffs to haunting cinematic soundscapes.

columns.title: Baritone Advantages
columns.text: Extended range without additional strings. Powerful low-end for heavy music. Unique tonal character in standard range. Perfect for down-tuned styles. Excellent string tension at low tunings.

cards.title: Scale Length
cards.description: The defining characteristic of baritone guitars is their extended scale length, typically 27-30 inches compared to standard guitars' 24.75-25.5 inches.

cards.title: Tuning Range
cards.description: Baritones are typically tuned a fourth or fifth lower than standard guitars, providing access to much deeper frequencies while maintaining playability.

fields.label: Standard Tuning
fields.value: E-A-D-G-B-E

fields.label: Baritone Standard
fields.value: B-E-A-D-F#-B

fields.label: Low Range
fields.value: Down to A or even lower

cards.title: Scale Length Options
items: 27" Scale: Shorter baritone scale, closer to standard guitar feel
28-28.5" Scale: Most common baritone scale length, balanced tension
30" Scale: Extended scale for maximum low-end clarity
Multi-Scale/Fanned: Different scale lengths per string for optimal tension

cards.title: Construction Differences
items: Reinforced Neck: Stronger construction to handle increased string tension
Larger Body: Often bigger than standard guitars for better low-end resonance
Heavy-Gauge Strings: Typically .013-.072 or heavier for proper tension
Adjusted Bracing: Internal bracing optimized for lower frequencies

fields.label: Tuning
fields.value: B-E-A-D-F#-B

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Most common baritone tuning. Perfect fourth down from standard guitar.

fields.label: Benefits
fields.value: Familiar chord shapes, easy transition from standard guitar

fields.label: Tuning
fields.value: A-E-A-D-F#-B

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Baritone version of drop D tuning. Lowest string tuned to A.

fields.label: Benefits
fields.value: Power chords on lowest two strings, heavy metal applications

fields.label: Tuning
fields.value: C-F-Bb-Eb-G-C

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Extended range tuning for maximum low end.

fields.label: Benefits
fields.value: Deep, powerful sound, extended range for composition

fields.label: Tuning
fields.value: E-A-D-G-B-E (octaved)

fields.label: Description
fields.value: Standard tuning with thinner strings tuned an octave higher.

fields.label: Benefits
fields.value: Chimey, bell-like tones, complements standard guitars

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Rich, woody low-end resonance; perfect for fingerpicking and folk; natural compression and sustain; ideal for songwriting and recording

fields.label: Best for
fields.value: Country, folk, Americana, cinematic music, solo performance

fields.label: Notable models
fields.value: Martin D-28BTE, Taylor Custom Baritone, Santa Cruz Baritone

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Aggressive attack and definition; perfect for heavy, distorted tones; extended range for lead work; effects processing possibilities

fields.label: Best for

cards.title: A Unique Instrument
cards.description: The Fender Bass VI, originally introduced in 1961, is perhaps the most famous baritone guitar. With its 30-inch scale and unique tuning (E-E, one octave below standard guitar), it occupies a special place between guitar and bass.

fields.label: Specifications
fields.value: 30" scale length; E-A-D-G-B-E tuning (octave below guitar); three single-coil pickups; Jaguar-style body and electronics; floating bridge with vibrato

fields.label: Famous Users
fields.value: The Beatles (various songs), The Cure (Robert Smith), Radiohead, Jack White, Peter Hook (New Order, Joy Division)

cards.title: Rhythm Techniques
items: Power chords: Massive, thick sound in low register
Open chords: Rich, complex voicings
Palm muting: Percussive attack for metal styles
Drone notes: Sustained low notes under melodies
Chord extensions: Use the extended range for unique voicings

cards.title: Lead Techniques
items: Extended range solos: Access to lower melodic register
Harmonic intervals: Rich two-note harmonies
Slide guitar: Excellent for atmospheric textures
Ambient picking: Spacious, cinematic soundscapes
Cross-picking: Complex fingerpicking patterns

cards.title: Setup Considerations
items: String gauge: Heavier strings needed for proper tension
Intonation: Critical due to extended scale length
Action height: May need adjustment for comfortable playing
Nut slots: Must accommodate heavier strings
Bridge adjustment: Important for tuning stability

fields.label: Familiar Territory
fields.value: Same chord shapes, different pitches; standard guitar techniques apply; familiar fretboard patterns; easy transition from 6-string guitar

fields.label: New Considerations
fields.value: Heavier string tension requires adjustment; extended scale affects finger stretches; different tonal palette to explore; may need to adjust playing style

cards.title: Practice Tips
items: Start with familiar songs: Learn songs you know in new tuning
Explore the low end: Take advantage of the extended range
Experiment with effects: Reverb and delay sound great on baritones
Play with others: Baritones complement standard guitars well
Record your playing: Hear how the baritone sits in a mix
